hypothesis_card.mechanism: AWS spot prices are step-administered per AZ around a family level; the pooled 730-day change-quantile band is symmetric-ish and calibrated to the AVERAGE series, but below-median AZs have positively skewed forward change distributions (reversion-up events, regional repricing waves) that the pooled q90 underestimates. Stretching only the upper quantile around the unchanged center (q90 = q50 + f*(q90-q50)) enlarges the breach allowance exactly where the empirical q90 breach rate is highest (35% at h180 on 2023-06..2024-03 pseudo-origins) without touching the q50 that the median-skill gate scores. Above-median series are left untouched because the dense backtest measured widening them loss-negative (-0.006 pooled, all hurt series premium p5).
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled skill rises from 0.2675 to ~0.273 (+0.0055), h180 +0.007 / h90 +0.006, h30 exactly unchanged (gate off), coverage_80 +0.013, q90 breach 24.6%->23.2% with q10 breach identical; dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest: pooled delta +0.0045, origin-bootstrap SE 0.0016, z=2.85, ~61% of origins improved, helped cells concentrated in below-median p4d AZs (apne1-az4 +0.0037, use2-az2 +0.0018), median skill delta only -0.002 (vs -0.011 ungated).
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The gain is not conditional tail calibration but a generic widening artifact: any q90 stretch would score well in the 2023-24 Discovery window because prices drifted up (the same "rising window rewards any uplift" rival the champion faced). Evidence against it: (a) the dense 33-origin backtest showed widening ABOVE-median (premium p5) series is loss-NEGATIVE (-0.006 pooled) while the identical widening below-median is +0.006 — a generic drift artifact would have rewarded both states; (b) the ungated variant's median skill fell -0.011 while the gated variant's fell only -0.002, so the gate, not the widening per se, carries the calibration; (c) q10 breach is byte-identical to the champion (8.5/13.4/5.3%), so no lower-tail trade was hidden.
hypothesis_card.test: Paired dry run on the 16 Discovery origins (pooled +0.0055, 9/16 origins improved, h90 +0.0057 / h180 +0.0071, h30 exactly 0.0) plus a dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest decomposing the lever: ungated widening +0.0064 pooled but median -0.011 (gate-2 risk), below-median-gated widening +0.0045 pooled / median -0.002 (committed), stronger factors {1.4/1.7} +0.0054 but median -0.006 (rejected on the gate-2 floor estimate 0.2675 < 0.2685), {1.3/1.7} +0.0051 / median -0.0051 (borderline, rejected). The 365d recent-window blend was tested and FALSIFIED on the scored window (dry run 2: -0.0048 pooled, screen FAIL, h180 -0.0106, origins 2024-07/08/09 -0.025/-0.047/-0.135).
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled skill <= champion (0.2675) or any sanity check fails (final: 0.2730, screen PASS). The conditional-tail hypothesis is falsified if the dense backtest delta is not significant (|z| < 2; measured z=2.85) or if the Holdout h90/h180 skills fall below the champion's (0.2226/0.3870) — i.e. the breach reduction does not transfer out of sample; also falsified if Holdout median skill < 0.2685 (gate-2 floor), which would mean the widening's q90-width cost to the median series outweighs the breach gain.

hypothesis: The champion's pooled 730-day h-day change quantiles under-cover the fat RIGHT tail of administered AWS spot repricing at 90-180 days (Discovery q90 breach 24.6% overall, 32.4% at h180; coverage_80 0.664 below the 0.70 hard band). The breach risk is concentrated in AZs priced BELOW their instance-family cross-sectional median — the same state the champion's confirmed reversion shift keys on — because their upside (reversion up, regional repricing) is fat while above-median premium series (p5/H100) have thin upside and fat DOWNSIDE. So stretching q90 away from q50 by a factor f (q90 <- q50 + f*(q90-q50), q10/q50 byte-identical) ONLY for below-median series at h>=90 (f=1.3 at h90, 1.5 at h180) cuts the q90 breach penalty (16-21% of long-horizon loss) at a small q90-width cost, and leaves the median skill essentially untouched.
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices at 90-180 days are administered around an instance-family level with fat upside risk concentrated in below-median AZs: AWS compresses spot discounts and rebalances reclaimed capacity (Capacity Blocks for ML, AWS News Blog 2023-10-31, aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml-to-reserve-gpu-capacity-for-your-machine-learning-workloads; re:Invent 2024 capacity-management recap, zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17d: "there has been a significant drop [in Spot prices] over the past year. We continue to look for ways to lower these prices further"), so cheap AZs revert up and their q90 must be stretched, while premium H100 (p5) series carry downside risk instead (Akash offering H100s at ~$2/hr vs AWS ~$12, gregosuri.com/predictions/gpu-economics/2024-06-13-2-hr-h100s-vs-amazon-s-12-r2mz/, shows premium-price fragility; AWS price-list churn of 65,388 cuts vs 259,823 increases, CostPulse 2024-08-02, costpulse.io/aws-price-changes/amazon-elastic-compute-cloud/20240802172840/, documents constant repricing). Two point-in-time Exa searches this episode found NO dated, quantifiable spot-drift news signal usable inside predict_origin (the CostPulse feed is RHEL-rate repricing noise, not instance prices; the Akash piece is a single anecdote), so the committed forecast is pack-only and the tail risk is captured by the empirical change quantiles instead. The view would change if AWS stopped compressing spot discounts (a broad price INCREASE leaving below-median AZs persistently cheap would falsify the fat-upside assumption), if a new GPU generation (p6/Blackwell) made current p5/p4d capacity monotonically cheaper (downside tail would then need the widening instead), or if the h180 q90 breach stayed >30% out of sample, which would mean the widening is too small rather than misdirected.
